next_step: Run a prospective matched evaluation on an independently sampled set of promised-family tasks. Compare the scaffold, source, dense Horner, and a conventional algorithm given the same thin representation; measure correctness, operation counts, and wall time on the same hardware. Separately account for acquisition and preparation costs.
decisive_observation: Whether the scaffold lowers total cost, including measured preparation cost amortized over the sampled tasks, against the strongest equally informed conventional baseline.

outcome_decisions.repeatable_net_reduction: Invest next in testing algebraic generalization beyond the sampled tasks.
outcome_decisions.no_reduction_or_higher_cost: Keep the scaffold as a correctness-checked artifact; redirect effort to alternative retained representations or narrower favorable workloads.
outcome_decisions.thin_representation_helps_both_equally: Do not credit the gain to learning; investigate representations where learned reuse adds value.
outcome_decisions.inconclusive: Refine the workload and measurement before making a broader claim.

retained_result: The scaffold's outputs match source and Horner at seven declared points; its observed operation counts are higher at those points. The thin representation has a conditional algebraic result.
uncertainty: Seven replay points do not establish workload-wide performance. Future-task distribution, wall time, acquisition cost, and any learning-specific advantage remain unknown.
